title: Joseph's Silver Cup

questions.question: What did Joseph's steward hide in Benjamin's sack?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:2: "Put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest."

questions.question: In whose sack was the cup found?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:12: "The cup was found in Benjamin's sack."

questions.question: What did the brothers do when the cup was found?
options: They tore their clothes and returned to the city
questions.correctAnswer: They tore their clothes and returned to the city
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:13: "Then they tore their clothes, and every man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city."

questions.question: What punishment did Joseph declare for the one who had the cup?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:17: "Only the man in whose hand the cup was found shall be my servant."

questions.question: Who pleaded with Joseph on behalf of Benjamin?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:18: "Then Judah went up to him and said, 'Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word.'"

questions.question: What did the brothers first say when accused of stealing?
options: Whoever has it shall die, and the rest will be slaves
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever has it shall die, and the rest will be slaves
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:9: "Whichever of your servants is found with it shall die, and we also will be my lord's servants."

questions.question: What did Judah say would happen if Benjamin did not return?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:31: "When he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die."

questions.question: What did Judah offer in place of Benjamin?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:33: "Please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord."

questions.question: What did Judah reveal about Jacob's feelings for Benjamin?
options: Jacob's life was bound up in the boy's life
Jacob wanted to send Benjamin away
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob's life was bound up in the boy's life
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:30: "His life is bound up in the boy's life."

questions.question: What did Joseph claim the silver cup was used for?
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:5: "Is it not from this that my lord drinks, and by this that he practices divination?"

questions.question: How did Judah's plea demonstrate his transformation?
options: He was willing to sacrifice himself for Benjamin, unlike when he sold Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: He was willing to sacrifice himself for Benjamin, unlike when he sold Joseph
questions.explanation: In Genesis 37, Judah suggested selling Joseph. Now in 44:33, he offers himself as a slave to protect Benjamin.

questions.question: What did Judah say Jacob told them about Rachel's sons?
options: One is gone and if harm comes to the other he would die
questions.correctAnswer: One is gone and if harm comes to the other he would die
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:27-29: Jacob said Rachel bore him two sons; one is gone, and if this one is taken too, it would bring his gray hairs to Sheol.

questions.question: What did the steward modify about the brothers' proposed punishment?
options: He said only the one with the cup would be a slave and the rest could go free
questions.correctAnswer: He said only the one with the cup would be a slave and the rest could go free
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:10: "Only the one who is found with it shall be my servant. But the rest of you shall be innocent."

questions.question: What did Judah say God had done?
options: Found out the guilt of your servants
questions.correctAnswer: Found out the guilt of your servants
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:16: "God has found out the guilt of your servants."

questions.question: In what order were the sacks searched?
options: From the eldest to the youngest
questions.correctAnswer: From the eldest to the youngest
questions.explanation: Genesis 44:12: "He searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest."

key_verse_text: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go back with his brothers.
